properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): opt-in was designed to finish by a process restart the CLIENT performs, and the instruction named one client's command; the latent process never re-probed or grew the surface, so on a client without that command genesis could not finish — the same class as the August signpost that instructed a party not in the room, and the in-place promotion the August restore report asked for was never built
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL on Anthony's "immediately", 2026-09-14, on fact:field-report-genesis-on-grok-build-cannot-finish-because-next-step-names-mcp-and-the-latent-server-is-never-replaced.

① OBSERVED (Alex, Grok Build TUI, reflow2-mcp 0.60.2, machine-wide --only-if-present): reflow2_start_design created an empty .reflow2/, returned started: true and next_step "Ask the user to run /mcp (reconnect the reflow2 server), then continue." Grok Build has /mcps and no reconnect. After "continue" the client re-queried the tool list and got the same two tools; a second call returned started: false with the same instruction; the stderr log showed the original latent process; .reflow2/graph was never created; genesis and report-friction could not run. Expected: one next step this client and this user could do, after which the full surface is served. NOT affected: the nearby-design check, describe_designs, and the directory creation all worked; the first six steps of the opt-in were sound.

② PRECEDENT, searched. fact:defect-the-latent-surface-never-re-probes-after-a-cli-restore (2026-08-15) asked, in order of preference: (a) re-probe on tool call and promote latent → full IN PLACE — "the latent server already knows the path it is watching"; (b) start_design detects a store appeared and says restart; (c) the blurb names the restart. Only (b) and (c) were built. fact:the-signpost-instructs-a-party-that-cannot-act-and-the-absent-client-was-named (2026-08-28) names the class: a mitigation that instructs the CLIENT while being read by the AGENT, who cannot change its harness. rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground (Anthony, 2026-08-26): reflow2 targets ANY MCP client; the only assumption is that the product can call an MCP server; slash commands are outside the line. fact:reflow2s-mechanisms-for-reaching-an-agent-are-mostly-claude-code-shaped. fact:defect-a-clients-tool-list-is-fixed-at-connection (2026-09-06).

③ CANDIDATES from the bones: (a) ALLOCATION — the opt-in's last step was allocated to the client (a process restart), not to the server. (b) CONTRACT — the instruction named one client's command (/mcp) as the way. (c) GOVERNANCE — the design rule forbids resting a mechanism on a slash command; nothing checks served strings for one. (d) ASSURANCE — no test drove the latent server through opt-in on a client-neutral path. (e) NOT IN THE SUSPECTED COMPONENT — Grok's /mcps refresh might replace the process (Alex never reached it). (f) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG — Grok did not re-query the tool list.

④/⑤ MEASURED 2026-09-14. (a) CONFIRMED in latent.rs: LatentService is a separate rmcp service with its own two-tool router; its own doc said "the design surface this session needs is served by a *different* process"; nothing re-probed on list_tools or call_tool; start_design deliberately opened no store. (b) CONFIRMED: two next_step strings, "run /mcp" and "fully restart this client (a /mcp reconnect is not always enough)". (c) CONFIRMED: the rule is advisory (enforced: false, his choice) and no lint reads served strings for client commands. (d) CONFIRMED: no test in crates/reflow2-mcp/tests or tools/ drove the latent server past opt-in. (e) NOT MEASURABLE here and made moot by the fix. (f) REFUTED by Alex's own step 5: search_tool after "continue" still listed two tools — the client asked again and the server had nothing new; the bottleneck was the process. And the mechanism to grow a surface inside MCP exists: rmcp 3.3.0 (the pinned version; a 3.1.2 copy in the registry cache is stale) has ServerCapabilities::enable_tool_list_changed and Peer::notify_tool_list_changed, i.e. notifications/tools/list_changed.

⑥ THE CLASS: a step that must complete on any MCP client was allocated to a party outside MCP — the client's own reconnect — and the instruction that carried it named one product's command. It is the 08-28 class (instruct a party not in the room) meeting the 08-15 class (a surface bound at startup is never re-examined). Would this fix have stopped the 08-15 report? Yes: it is option (a) from that report, built. Would it have stopped this one? Yes on every step: the store is opened by the process that opted the directory in, the client is told the list changed, and the next step names no command as the way.

⑦ PINNED FIRST: tools/test_latent_promotion.py, four tests over the real binary on stdio with a client-neutral clientInfo — the latent tools before opt-in; start_design promotes this same process (store created, notifications/tools/list_changed received, tools/list shows add_project and get_skill, get_skill genesis answers, next_step contains no "run /mcp"); a second start_design says the surface is served; a store that appears underneath (the restore case) is served on the next call. Three of four observed failing against the 0.60.2 binary.

⑧ FIXED AT THE CAUSE: LatentService re-probes on every list_tools and call_tool; when the design directory exists it opens the store once (ReflowService::new_reporting) and delegates every call except reflow2_start_design to the full service; start_design promotes in the same call and sends notifications/tools/list_changed; the capability is declared at the handshake; next_step says the surface is SERVED NOW by this same server and names a client restart only as the fallback, with per-product hints (Claude Code /mcp, Grok Build /mcps, any other: restart) riding as additions, which is what the rule allows. The CI runs the promotion test against the built binary.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether Grok Build honours tools/list_changed (Alex's step 5 shows it re-queries after a turn, which is enough either way); whether any other client caches the list until restart — the fallback line covers it and says so; the two hooks and slash commands that remain Claude-Code-shaped are unchanged and out of scope; the advisory rule still has no lint for client commands in served strings, recorded as the detector leg not built.
